notes: Every screen is new. Home is one card: today's workout with each lift's target and Start, a protein tile, the weigh-in, what's due, your streaks. Workout walks you through one lift and one set at a time with a rest clock that keeps running on every tab and buzzes at zero; All lifts shows the whole session (Full, 45 or 30 minutes, drag to reorder) and the day name swaps days. Food is one box (type, talk or snap a photo) with chips for the foods you log most. Progress is three numbers, your weight trend, your main lifts, sets by muscle and photos, with charts, check-in forms, milestones and settings behind the gear. Pick your own accent color. All your data stays as it is. 3.3.1: the cycle-notes tap is back on Home. 3.3.2: on the week sheet, tap a day then tap where it goes, or hold and drag; swaps are for this week only, with a warning when two hard days would touch and an Undo. 3.3.3: Log set keeps you on the lift until its sets are in. The lb and reps boxes start empty with the suggestion in grey, so typing replaces it, and after your first set the grey numbers show the set you just did. What you type saves on its own and the keyboard stays open. The button always says Log set, the two Skip buttons now say Skip rest and Skip lift, and a line tells you when you're on a day other than today. The menu is now Home, Food, Workout, Progress, and the badge at the bottom is gone. 3.4.0: at meal time, Food offers your usual meal or the same meal as yesterday, logged in one tap. Amount buttons (½×, 1½×, 2×) after a chip and on the Save card. Quick add takes just calories and protein. Light days are left out of your weekly averages. A warm-up line before your first heavy set, a fun weight line and a compare-to-last-time line on the finish card, Today's lifts (was All lifts), and day swaps that move right away with Undo.
knowledgeNotes: New training knowledge: a plan-building playbook (weekly sets by goal, effort, progression, deload ranges), a recommendation guide (fixes and options for common feedback), and an exercise A to Z of extra exercises for each muscle group. Your coach uses it quietly when you ask for a change. Say "turn on plan review" if you want it to suggest plan updates.
